segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: First-deviation probe: raw readings were in-band, the unit had just been overhauled, and continuing while monitoring felt more reasonable than easing off and inspecting after the investment in the unit.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant links the continue-versus-inspect choice to the recent costly overhaul and time already invested, beyond the in-band readings alone.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Green-band probe: the monitoring readout was clean, a manual sample was available, and the participant regarded manual checking as merely confirming what the instruments already said.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The automated green-band readout was treated as sufficient confirmation in place of available manual verification.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Fuel-filter probe: attention remained on the turbocharger; the filter note was acknowledged but deferred because it lacked a fuel or combustion symptom.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A competing differential-pressure cue was registered but not processed for action because attention was fixed on the turbocharger.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Bearing-failure probe: after comparing diversion with a jury-rig, the participant said the overhaul cost and troubleshooting time already spent made diversion feel wasteful on top of the schedule hit.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The decision to continue at reduced load was justified by prior money and time investment rather than only the present risk and repair options.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Time-pressure and confidence response: confidence varied from running-in to no concern to reduced confidence at failure, while the tide window narrowed the options.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This explains confidence and operational pressure but does not independently manifest one of the hidden target mechanisms.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Missing-information response: an alarm or metal particulates in an early manual sample would have triggered action, but the instruments did not provide that trigger.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant identifies an evidence threshold that would have changed the decision; this is not itself a hidden bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Looking-back reflection: the initial vibration was described as probably indicating the bearing problem from the start and fairly clear in hindsight, rather than bedding in.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: After learning the outcome, the participant recasts the originally ambiguous in-band signal as clearly predictive of the failure.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: No-tide-window counterfactual: without the deadline, diverting might have felt cleaner because it would not carry the same schedule cost.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a schedule-pressure counterfactual and does not by itself establish a hidden cognitive-bias instance.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The finding localizes to the first-deviation segment and describes the overhaul shaping the running-in interpretation, but its confirmation-bias label and mechanism do not capture the hidden instance's defining use of prior investment as a reason to continue rather than inspect. obs_002 is the one-to-one match for that hidden instance.

The quote and mechanism fully match the competing-cue attentional mechanism, so this finding is credited as a mechanism-first TP for MO5_SA_01. The label is a near neighbor rather than an approved equivalent, making it a strict FP while the hidden instance remains a strict FN.

The prediction is located in the correct broad bearing-failure decision segment and is supported as a schedule-pressure interpretation, but the hidden target requires prior-investment weighting. It does not state or match that mechanism. obs_006 is the one-to-one match for MO5_SC_02.

candidates.details: The exact retrospective quote recasts an initially ambiguous signal as clearly predictive with outcome knowledge. The caveat that the participant used probabilistic language is a reasonable alternative interpretation, but the quote and stated candidate mechanism meet the supplied hidden-instance criteria when the candidate tier is scored.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Strict and mechanism-first TP counts rise from 1 to 3, with 2 additional false positives; segment hits rise from 1 to 3. F1 rises from 0.3333 to 0.6000 for both instance scorecards.

Mechanism-first F1 rises to 0.7273 and strict F1 becomes 0.5455.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: The hindsight candidate adds one strict and one mechanism-first TP without an extra FP; segment hits rise from 4 to 5. Strict F1 rises to 0.6667 and mechanism-first F1 to 0.8333.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high-and-moderate threshold, 3 of 5 positive segments are detected, with no false alarms (segment F1 0.7500). All identified-confidence findings detect 4 of 5 positive segments; adding candidates detects all 5.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high and moderate, 3 of 5 hidden instances match strictly, with 2 false-positive findings and 2 missed instances (precision 0.6000, recall 0.6000, F1 0.6000). All confidence levels retain 3 TPs, with 3 FPs; the hindsight candidate raises the fourth-threshold result to 4 TPs and 1 FN.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high and moderate, 3 of 5 hidden mechanisms match (F1 0.6000). Including low confidence adds the selective-attention mechanism for 4 TPs; including the hindsight candidate yields 5 TPs, 2 FPs, and F1 0.8333.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The single hindsight candidate is a useful cautious detection: it remains unscored at the first three thresholds and becomes a strict and mechanism-first TP only when candidates are included.
main_failure_modes: The first-deviation mechanism is reported as confirmation bias rather than the hidden sunk-cost instance; its described mechanism overlaps only partially, while the separate sunk-cost finding correctly matches that instance.
The fuel-filter finding uses the near-neighbor label attentional tunneling: it is a mechanism-first TP but a strict label FP.
The added plan-continuation finding is an extra strict FP; its schedule-pressure mechanism does not match the hidden sunk-cost mechanism at the same broad decision segment.
Hindsight bias is present only as a candidate, so it is missed at the first three thresholds.
main_strengths: The moderate sunk-cost and automation-bias findings use valid interview evidence and match their hidden mechanisms.
The high-confidence post-failure sunk-cost finding captures the second planned occurrence distinctly.
The candidate tier preserves uncertainty while recovering the hidden hindsight instance at the fourth threshold.
All quoted evidence is traceable to the raw interview; no retrieved support is claimed.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: The run shows solid segment-level detection and mechanism coverage, with threshold-dependent gains from low-confidence and candidate findings. Strict label scoring is reduced by one near-neighbor attentional label, a confirmation-bias relabeling of the first sunk-cost episode, and an extra plan-continuation prediction. The candidate tier adds the hindsight instance without adding a false positive.
